result:
Solution 3 gives the correct answer, 30.

Solution 1 assumes the cohomology vanishes exactly when the genus of $X_0(p)$ is zero, but then lists $p=2,3,5,7$ and omits $p=13$. $X_0(13)$ has genus 0, so 13 belongs in the set. Its sum of 17 is therefore wrong.

Solution 2 cites a vanishing set $\{2,3,5\}$ that doesn't match the genus-zero description of the Γ₀-type case, so its sum of 10 is wrong.

Solution 3 identifies the top cohomology with weight-2 modular symbols for $\Gamma_0(p)$, whose dimension is the genus $g(X_0(p))$. The genus of $X_0(p)$ is zero exactly for $p \in \{2,3,5,7,13\}$, which gives $2+3+5+7+13 = 30$. This matches my recollection of the Miller–Patzt–Putman result for $\Gamma_{0,3}^+(p)$, though I have not re-derived it. Its intermediate computations are sketchy, for example the claimed $\dim H^3(\Gamma_0(11);\mathbb{Q}) = 2$ is not checked here, but the final set is correct.

CHOICE: 3
